unit: Ch 5: Set-Off or Carry Forward and Set-off of Losses
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Concept of Set-Off and Inter-Source Adjustment
explain: Set-off means adjusting losses incurred in a source or head against eligible taxable income in the same tax year.
Inter-source set-off allows loss from one source to be adjusted against income from another source under the same head of income.
Long-term capital loss (LTCL) can only be set off against long-term capital gains (LTCG), not short-term capital gains.
Short-term capital loss (STCL) can be set off against both short-term capital gains (STCG) and long-term capital gains (LTCG).
Losses from an exempt income source cannot be set off against any taxable income from any source.

flow.title: Inter-Source Set-Off Process
steps: Identify loss under a specific head
Check if income exists under same head
Apply inter-source restrictions like LTCL rule
Set off loss against eligible source income

topics.example: A loss of Rs. 50,000 from a textile business can be set off against Rs. 80,000 profit from a printing business in the same tax year.
remember: Loss from an exempt source cannot be set off against taxable income.
mistakes: Attempting to set off long-term capital loss against short-term capital gains.

quiz.q: Under Section 108(2), long-term capital loss can be set off against:
quiz.why: Section 108(2) restricts the set-off of long-term capital loss strictly against long-term capital gains.

quiz.q: Can a loss from an exempt source of income be set off against taxable income?
o: No, loss from exempt source cannot be set off
Yes, if approved by Assessing Officer
quiz.why: If income from a source is exempt from tax, loss from that exempt source cannot be set off against any taxable income.

topics.title: Inter-Head Adjustment
explain: Inter-head adjustment allows loss under one head of income to be set off against income under another head in the same tax year.
Loss under the head Profits and Gains of Business or Profession cannot be set off against income under the head Salaries.
Loss under the head Capital Gains cannot be set off against income under any other head.
Under the optional tax regime, loss from house property can be set off against other heads only up to a maximum of Rs. 2,00,000.
Under the default tax regime u/s 202(1), house property loss cannot be set off against any other head of income.
No loss can be set off against casual income like lotteries, crossword puzzles, card games, or betting u/s 94.

flow.title: Inter-Head Set-Off Steps
steps: Compute net loss remaining after inter-source set-off
Verify head-specific restrictions
Ensure business loss avoids Salaries head
Limit house property set-off per regime
Set off against remaining eligible heads

topics.example: A business loss of Rs. 40,000 can be set off against house property income of Rs. 1,00,000, but cannot touch salary income of Rs. 3,00,000.
remember: Maximum house property loss set-off against other heads is Rs. 2,00,000 under the optional regime.
mistakes: Setting off business losses against salary income.

quiz.q: Under Section 109, business loss cannot be set off against income under which head?
quiz.why: Section 109 specifically debars setting off PGBP business losses against Salary income.

quiz.q: Under the default tax regime u/s 202(1), loss from house property:
o: Can be set off up to Rs. 2 lakhs
Can be set off without limit
Cannot be set off against any other head
Can be set off against salary only
quiz.why: Under default tax regime u/s 202(1), house property loss is not allowed to be set off against any other head.

topics.title: Carry Forward & Set-Off of Loss from House Property
explain: Unabsorbed loss under the head Income from House Property can be carried forward only if the assessee opts out of the default tax regime.
Once carried forward, house property loss can be set off ONLY against income under the head Income from House Property in succeeding years.
The maximum period for carrying forward unabsorbed house property loss is 8 tax years immediately succeeding the year of loss.
Under the default tax regime u/s 202(1), house property loss cannot be set off against other heads and cannot be carried forward to subsequent years.

flow.title: House Property Loss Carry Forward Process
steps: Determine unabsorbed house property loss
Check regime selected by assessee
If optional regime carry forward loss
Set off against future house property income
Enforce maximum 8 tax years limit

topics.example: Unabsorbed house property loss of Rs. 20,000 under the optional tax regime is carried forward to set off against house property income of the following tax year.
remember: Maximum carry forward period for house property loss is 8 tax years under optional regime.
mistakes: Attempting to carry forward house property loss under the default tax regime.

quiz.q: What is the maximum carry forward period for unabsorbed house property loss under section 110?
quiz.why: Section 110 allows unabsorbed house property loss to be carried forward up to a maximum of 8 tax years.

quiz.q: Once house property loss is carried forward to a subsequent tax year, it can be set off against:
quiz.why: In succeeding tax years, carried forward house property loss can only be set off against income under the head House Property.

topics.title: Carry Forward & Set-Off of Capital Losses
explain: Net loss under the head Capital Gains cannot be set off against any other head of income in the current year.
Unabsorbed short-term capital loss (STCL) carried forward can be set off against short-term or long-term capital gains in future years.
Unabsorbed long-term capital loss (LTCL) carried forward can be set off ONLY against long-term capital gains in future years.
Both STCL and LTCL can be carried forward for a maximum period of 8 tax years immediately succeeding the year of loss.
Long-term capital loss on shares/units (where STT is paid) can also be carried forward and set off against long-term capital gains.

flow.title: Capital Loss Carry Forward and Set-Off
steps: Identify net unabsorbed capital loss
Classify loss into STCL or LTCL
Carry forward up to 8 tax years
Set off STCL against STCG or LTCG
Set off LTCL against LTCG only

topics.example: Brought forward LTCL of Rs. 96,000 is set off against current year LTCG of Rs. 75,000, leaving Rs. 21,000 LTCL to be carried forward to the next year.
remember: Maximum carry forward period for capital losses (STCL and LTCL) is 8 tax years.
mistakes: Setting off brought forward LTCL against current year short-term capital gains.

quiz.q: Carried forward short-term capital loss can be set off against:
o: Both short-term and long-term capital gains
quiz.why: Carried forward STCL can be set off against income under the head Capital Gains (both STCG and LTCG).

quiz.q: Unabsorbed capital losses under Section 111 can be carried forward for a maximum period of:
quiz.why: Section 111 provides that unabsorbed short-term or long-term capital losses can be carried forward for a maximum of 8 tax years.

topics.title: Carry Forward & Set-Off of Non-Speculative Business Losses
explain: Non-speculative business loss not fully set off in the current year against eligible heads (excluding salary) can be carried forward.
Carried forward business loss can be set off ONLY against Profits and Gains of Business or Profession in subsequent tax years.
It can be set off against income of any business or profession, not necessarily the same business in which the loss was incurred.
Only the person who incurred the business loss is entitled to carry it forward and set it off, except in cases of succession by inheritance.
The maximum period for carry forward of non-speculative business loss is 8 tax years immediately succeeding the year of loss.

flow.title: Non-Speculative Business Loss Flow
steps: Compute net business loss after current set-offs
Verify loss is non-speculative
Check continuity of assessee identity
Carry forward for maximum 8 tax years
Set off against future business profits only

topics.example: Brought forward textile business loss of Rs. 50,000 from 5 years ago can be set off against current year leather business profit of Rs. 1,00,000.
remember: Maximum carry forward period for non-speculative business loss is 8 tax years.
mistakes: Attempting to set off carried forward business loss against salary or house property income in a future year.

quiz.q: Carried forward business loss under section 112 can be set off in subsequent years against:
o: Income under any head of income
Profits and gains of business or profession
quiz.why: Carried forward business loss can only be set off against profits and gains of business or profession.

quiz.q: What is the maximum period for carrying forward unabsorbed non-speculative business loss?
quiz.why: Section 112(v) mandates a maximum carry forward period of 8 tax years for non-speculative business losses.

topics.title: Losses in Speculation Business
explain: Speculation business is treated as distinct and separate from any other non-speculative business.
Loss incurred in a speculation business can be set off ONLY against profits and gains of another speculation business.
Where part of a company's business consists of buying and selling shares of other companies, it is deemed carrying on speculation business (with specific exceptions for banking/finance companies).
Losses from derivative trading are not treated as speculative losses.
Unabsorbed speculation business loss can be carried forward for a maximum period of 4 tax years immediately succeeding the year of loss.

flow.title: Speculation Loss Set-Off Procedure
steps: Identify loss from speculative transaction
Check for current speculation business profits
Set off against current speculation profits only
Carry forward unabsorbed loss up to 4 years
Set off only against future speculation profits

topics.example: Loss of Rs. 85,000 from speculation business X is set off against Rs. 45,000 profit from speculation business Y, leaving Rs. 40,000 to be carried forward.
remember: Maximum carry forward period for speculation loss is 4 tax years.
mistakes: Setting off speculation loss against normal non-speculation business income.

quiz.q: Loss from a speculation business can be set off against:
quiz.why: Under Section 113(1), speculation business loss can only be set off against profits of another speculation business.

quiz.q: What is the maximum period for carry forward of speculative business loss under section 113?
quiz.why: Section 113(iv) limits the carry forward of speculation loss to a maximum of 4 tax years.

topics.title: Carry Forward & Set-Off of Specified Business Losses
explain: Specified business refers to businesses claiming deduction under Section 46 (e.g., operating hospitals or hotels).
Loss from a specified business u/s 46 can be set off ONLY against profits and gains of any other specified business.
This set-off rule applies when an assessee exercises the option of shifting out of the default tax regime and claims deduction u/s 46.
Losses from specified business under Section 46 can be carried forward for an INDEFINITE period.
If an assessee pays tax under the default regime u/s 202(1), Section 46 deduction is unavailable, making any resulting loss a normal business loss u/s 112.

flow.title: Specified Business Loss Carry Forward
steps: Identify loss from Section 46 specified business
Check assessee tax regime choice
Set off against other specified business profits
Carry forward remaining loss indefinitely
Set off against future specified business profits

topics.example: Loss of Rs. 20,000 from a new hospital business u/s 46 is carried forward indefinitely to set off against future specified business profits.
remember: Specified business loss u/s 46 can be carried forward for an INDEFINITE period.
mistakes: Assuming specified business loss has an 8-year limit like normal business loss.

quiz.q: Unabsorbed loss from specified business under section 46 can be carried forward for:
quiz.why: Section 114(ii) specifies no time limit, allowing specified business loss to be carried forward indefinitely.

quiz.q: Under the optional tax regime, loss from a specified business u/s 46 can be set off against:
o: Profits of another specified business only
quiz.why: Specified business loss can only be set off against profits and gains of another specified business.

topics.title: Losses from Specified Activity - Owning and Maintaining Race Horses
explain: Specified activity is defined strictly as the activity of owning and maintaining race horses.
Loss from specified activity can be set off ONLY against income from specified activity (owning and maintaining race horses).
Loss from owning race horses must not be confused with casual winnings from horse races (betting).
No loss can be set off against casual winnings (lotteries, crossword puzzles, card games, betting) u/s 94.
Unabsorbed loss from specified activity can be carried forward for a maximum period of 4 tax years immediately succeeding the year of loss.

flow.title: Race Horse Maintenance Loss Handling
steps: Calculate stake money minus maintenance expenditure
Identify net loss from owning race horses
Set off only against race horse maintenance income
Carry forward unabsorbed loss up to 4 years
Set off against future race horse income

topics.example: Brought forward loss of Rs. 25,000 from maintaining race horses is set off against current year race horse income of Rs. 15,000, leaving Rs. 10,000 carried forward.
remember: Loss from specified activity can be carried forward for a maximum of 4 tax years.
mistakes: Setting off loss from maintaining race horses against casual lottery winnings or general business income.

quiz.q: Loss incurred in the activity of owning and maintaining race horses can be set off against:
quiz.why: Section 115(1) restricts set-off of race horse maintenance loss strictly to income from specified activity.

quiz.q: What is the maximum carry forward period for loss from specified activity u/s 115?
quiz.why: Unabsorbed loss from specified activity (owning and maintaining race horses) can be carried forward for max 4 tax years.

topics.title: Order of Set-Off of Losses and Unabsorbed Depreciation
explain: When an assessee has current year business profits along with multiple brought forward deductions and losses, a specific statutory priority order must be followed.
Priority 1: Current year depreciation [Section 33(1)] and current year capital expenditure on scientific research/family planning.
Priority 2: Brought forward loss from business or profession [Section 112(1)].
Priority 3: Unabsorbed depreciation [Section 33(11)].
Priority 4: Unabsorbed capital expenditure on scientific research [Section 45(7)].
Priority 5: Unabsorbed expenditure on family planning [Section 32(i)].
Unabsorbed depreciation is added to current year depreciation u/s 33(11)(b) and can be set off against income under any head except Salaries.

flow.title: Priority Order of Set-Off
steps: Deduct current year depreciation
Deduct current capital exp on scientific research
Set off brought forward business loss
Set off unabsorbed depreciation
Set off unabsorbed capital scientific research exp
Set off unabsorbed family planning exp

topics.example: From gross business income, current year depreciation of Rs. 26,000 is deducted first, followed by brought forward business loss of Rs. 45,000, before applying unabsorbed depreciation.
remember: Brought forward business loss is set off BEFORE unabsorbed depreciation.
mistakes: Setting off unabsorbed depreciation before brought forward business loss.

quiz.q: What is the correct priority order for set-off among current depreciation, brought forward business loss, and unabsorbed depreciation?
o: B/f business loss, Current depreciation, Unabsorbed depreciation
Current depreciation, B/f business loss, Unabsorbed depreciation
Unabsorbed depreciation, Current depreciation, B/f business loss
Current depreciation, Unabsorbed depreciation, B/f business loss
quiz.why: Under section 112 order of priority, Current year depreciation comes 1st, Brought forward business loss 2nd, and Unabsorbed depreciation 3rd.

quiz.q: Unabsorbed depreciation brought forward under Section 33(11) can be set off against income under any head EXCEPT:
quiz.why: Unabsorbed depreciation becomes part of current year depreciation and can be set off against any head except Salaries.

topics.title: Mandatory Submission of Return of Losses
explain: To carry forward specified losses, the assessee MUST file a return of loss under Section 263(1) within the prescribed due date.
Losses requiring timely return filing: Capital loss u/s 111(1), Business loss u/s 112(1), Speculation loss u/s 113(2), Specified business loss u/s 114(2), and Specified activity loss u/s 115(2).
Exception 1: House property loss carried forward u/s 110 does NOT require timely return filing under Section 263(1).
Exception 2: Unabsorbed depreciation carried forward u/s 33(11) does NOT require timely return filing under Section 263(1).
If a return of loss is submitted after the due date, specified business, capital, speculative, and race horse losses cannot be carried forward.

flow.title: Return Filing Condition for Carrying Forward Losses
steps: Identify the loss incurred in tax year
Check if loss is house property or depreciation
If other loss file return on time
If filed within due date allow carry forward
If filed late deny loss carry forward

topics.example: Mr. Naveen files his loss return after the due date; his business loss of Rs. 55,000 CANNOT be carried forward, but unabsorbed depreciation of Rs. 1,00,000 CAN be carried forward.
remember: House property loss and unabsorbed depreciation CAN be carried forward even if return is filed late.
mistakes: Assuming house property loss cannot be carried forward if the return is filed late.

quiz.q: Which of the following losses can be carried forward EVEN IF the return of income is filed after the due date u/s 263(1)?
o: Loss under the head Capital Gains
quiz.why: Section 121 exempts house property loss u/s 110 and unabsorbed depreciation u/s 33(11) from the timely return filing condition.

quiz.q: Under Section 121, if a non-speculative business loss return is filed after the due date specified u/s 263(1):
o: The loss can be set off next year
The loss cannot be carried forward
The loss can be carried forward for 4 years
The loss carries a penalty of 10%
quiz.why: Section 121 mandates that business loss cannot be carried forward if the return is not filed within the due date.
